BUILT, on the people-and-life branch (src/simulation/living-world/political-reflection.ts): a person meets a question when they file a bill or are told about one; people who met a bill think it over again when it is signed, vetoed, enacted or dies; and VIEW_TRIGGERS is a table of life events that bring back questions a person has met, by policy domain. A new row needs no code. Its one row is the owner's own example: a serious or chronic illness of the person, or of close family who know about it, brings back health and human services questions.
PLACEHOLDER PACING (REFLECTION_PACE): half of meetings are thought over the next day, 35% within two to seven days, and 15% are left until something later brings the question back.

Candidate triggers not yet built, for the owner to confirm or strike: going to a rally or a party meeting; losing a job or a workplace closing; a tax bill or a rent or price rise; a disaster in their county and how it was handled; a child starting or leaving school, or a school closing; a crime against them or someone close; a death in the family; a move to another state; becoming a parent; turning eighteen and being registered to vote; a news story they read; an argument with someone whose view they respect.
question: What in a person's life starts them thinking about a political question, or brings one back, and how long do people take to settle where they stand? For each kind of event: which policy areas it bears on, whose life it reaches (only theirs, or family and friends who know about it), and how often it actually changes or firms up a view.

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: It names the first occasions (conversation, report, office briefing, experience of a policy) and says to reconsider when new facts arrive, but not the list of life events, what each bears on, or the pace.
It covers what an event does to a person, not which political questions it brings to mind.

title: What starts a political view, and how long it takes
usableAnswer: A list of life events, each with the policy domains it bears on (from the game's 13 state-and-local domains), whether it reaches only the person or also close family and friends who know, and a rough likelihood that it firms up or changes a view. A distribution for how long people take to settle a view after first meeting a question, including how often they never do until something else happens. The owner's own answers to which triggers belong in the game come first.
whyItMatters: Views now form in play and can come back when something happens, but only two triggers exist and the pacing is a guess. The owner wants more ways, variable timing, and to be asked.
